topicName: Idempotency and Distributed Locks in Jobs
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Idempotency and Distributed Locks in Ruby on Rails"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Background jobs are essential for scaling Ruby on Rails applications. However, handling concurrent executions, duplicate webhook deliveries, and network retries requires robust strategies. This tutorial explores implementing idempotency and distributed locks to ensure reliable background processing."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"The Problem of Duplicate Job Execution"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Background job queues like Sidekiq guarantee at-least-once delivery. This means network partitions, timeouts, or worker crashes can trigger the same job multiple times. Without safeguards, this leads to duplicate database records, double charges, or race conditions."},{"order":5,"type":"subheading","text":"Designing for Idempotency"},{"order":6,"type":"paragraph","text":"An idempotent operation can be applied multiple times without changing the result beyond the initial application. In Rails, we achieve this by checking the state before performing mutations or by using unique database constraints."},{"order":7,"type":"code","text":"class ProcessPaymentJob < ApplicationJob
  queue_as :default

  def perform(payment_id)
    payment = Payment.find(payment_id)
    return if payment.completed? || payment.failed?

    PaymentGateway.charge(payment)
    payment.update!(status: 'completed')
  rescue => e
    payment.update!(status: 'failed')
    raise e
  end
end"},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing Distributed Locks with Redis"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"When multiple workers attempt to process the same resource concurrently, check-then-act logic is vulnerable to race conditions. A distributed lock ensures that only one worker processes a specific job or resource at a time. The 'redis-lock' or 'redlock-rb' gems are standard choices."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"class SyncUserAccountJob < ApplicationJob
  include Redlock

  def perform(user_id)
    lock_key = "lock:user_sync:#{user_id}"
    redis = Redis.new
    lock_manager = Redlock::Client.new([redis])

    # Try to acquire lock for 5 seconds
    lock_manager.lock(lock_key, 5000) do |locked|
      if locked
        user = User.find(user_id)
        user.sync_with_external_api!
      else
        # Retry the job later if lock is held
        self.class.set(wait: 2.seconds).perform_later(user_id)
      end
    end
  end
end"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Best Practices for Production Rails Apps"},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Always add unique database indexes for transactional idempotency keys."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Set appropriate TTL (Time-To-Live) values on distributed locks to prevent deadlocks if a worker dies."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Log idempotency skips to monitor duplicate job generation and tune your retry logic."}]
